name: Hash Table Operations
description: Demonstrates fundamental hash table operations: insert, search, and delete using a simple hash function with separate chaining for collision handling.
aim: Implement O(1) average-time insert, search, and delete using a hash function to map keys to bucket indices, with chaining to handle collisions.
howItWorks: Choose table size (prime number reduces collisions)
Insert: compute index, add to bucket chain
Search: compute index, scan chain for key
Delete: compute index, remove from chain
Load factor = n/m; rehash when load factor > threshold

time.averageCase: With good hash function and load factor < 0.75
time.worstCase: All keys hash to same bucket — degenerates to linked list

complexity.spaceDescription: O(n) for n key-value pairs plus table array

realWorld: Python dict and Java HashMap implementation
Caches — fast O(1) lookup by key
Compiler symbol tables — variable name lookup
whenToUse: Frequent insert, delete, search operations needed
O(1) average performance more important than worst-case
alternatives: BST/Red-Black Tree — O(log n) guaranteed, ordered iteration
Trie — for string keys with prefix operations
Perfect hashing — O(1) worst case for static key sets
